slides.title: Copilot lifted productivity and renewal in the beta, but volunteer accounts flatter both results

claims.claim: Beta accounts scheduled more jobs per dispatcher-hour than matched accounts
evidence: +9 pp
Change in jobs per dispatcher-hour, prior 12 weeks: Beta accounts 0.11; Matched non-beta accounts 0.02

claims.claim: Beta accounts also renewed more often over 90 days
evidence: +4 pp
90-day renewal rate: Beta accounts 0.97; Matched non-beta accounts 0.93

claims.claim: Treat both gains as a ceiling: beta accounts volunteered, are more active and average 8.1 seats, against 6.2 across the base
evidence: Free beta of 240 volunteer accounts over 12 weeks; dispatchers also reported saving 4.1 hours a week (self-reported, no comparison group)
Whether the gain holds beyond volunteers is an open question in the briefing pack

slides.title: Asked to pay $149, only 14% of beta accounts bought Copilot, against the 46% the survey promised

claims.claim: Stated intent overstates real buying more than three times over
evidence: Share of accounts choosing Copilot at $149 per account per month: Said likely to buy at $149 (survey, n = 610) 0.46; Bought at $149 (paywall test, n = 120) 0.14
Survey: 6% replied, averaging 9.4 seats against 6.2; the paywall's 17 buyers were volunteers, so 14% is a ceiling

claims.claim: CPO case: 46% of 9,800 accounts = $8.1M
Paywall: 14% of 8,428 after churn = $2.1M

slides.title: Even at the tested purchase rate, heavy-using buyers leave the add-on only about $0.6M of gross profit a year

claims.claim: Add-on gross profit, first full year: $2.1M − $0.9M − $0.6M = $0.6M
evidence: $2.1M new ARR: 14% of the 8,428 accounts left after churn, × $1,788 a year
$0.9M inference: buyers send 6,800 requests a month at $0.009, or $61.20 an account
$0.6M platform, evaluation and support cost a year (briefing pack)
$0.6M gross profit a year, before the one-time build cost

claims.claim: The estimate is generous to the add-on
evidence: Buyers convert at the beta's 14%, although beta accounts volunteered and are larger and more active than the base
Buyers keep their test usage; the heaviest tenth of beta accounts average 14,500 requests a month
Inference stays at the contract price of $0.009 a request, fixed through December 2027
Uptake is counted at its full-year level; first-year revenue is lower while buyers sign up

claims.claim: A price per account draws the heaviest users: inference would absorb 41% of the add-on's revenue

slides.title: Even if AI explains the whole drop in win rate, Copilot wins back a third of the deals the memo claims

claims.claim: Copilot wins back a third of the deals the memo claims
evidence: Routewise deals a year: Sales memo: a third of lost Routewise deals 327.6; Whole drop in win rate, 44% to 37% 109.2
Routewise competes in about 60% of 2,600 qualified opportunities a year; a new account averages 6.2 seats on Core at $79

claims.claim: $0.6M new-customer ARR a year at most, if Copilot won back every deal lost to the drop; none of it counts toward NRR
Sales memo: 31% of loss notes mention AI, but a mention is not the reason a deal was lost
Other cause: Routewise also offered 20% off the first year in Q3 2026, the quarter its AI launched
For Brightwork: Copilot defends new deals; it is not the growth engine the memo implies

slides.title: Mobile reliability, not AI, is why customers leave: it drives 4.5 times as much churn as AI features

claims.claim: Mobile reliability drives 4.5 times as much churn as AI features
evidence: Main reason given by churned accounts, 2026 (n = 1,190): Mobile app reliability 0.27; Price 0.22; Other 0.16; Missing integrations 0.15; Went out of business / sold 0.14; Switched for AI features 0.06
Mobile compared with AI as a reason: 4.5x

claims.claim: The mobile delay has a cost that Copilot does not offset
evidence: Requests agree: 38% rank a reliable mobile app first, against 19% for AI scheduling
ARR lost a year to mobile reliability: $2.2M (27% × 14% logo churn × $57.6M ARR)
ARR lost a year to AI features: $0.5M (6% × 14% logo churn × $57.6M ARR)
ARR lost assumes churned accounts are of average size; it is a ceiling for what fixing each reason could save

6.2 office seats per account, the base average
